item.text:
Embed the torsion-free module \(M\) into \(M_K=K\otimes_R M\), where \(K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)\), and extend \(T\) \(K\)-linearly. This converts the problem to the familiar field case.

Organize the argument around two points:

1. For finite \(k,l\), the polynomials
   \[
   (X-\lambda)^k,\qquad (X-\mu)^l
   \]
   are coprime in \(K[X]\). A Bézout identity, evaluated at \(T\), forces any vector killed by both operators to vanish.

2. Treat depth \(\infty\) elementwise: membership in an unbounded generalized eigenspace supplies some finite exponent killing the given vector, reducing the claim to the finite-depth case.

Torsion-freeness is essential to this route because it makes \(M\to K\otimes_R M\) injective; without it, powers of the nonzero scalar \(\lambda-\mu\) could annihilate nonzero vectors.
